nodes.label: Look toward both sides for entering vehicles or pedestrians, especially near intersections and railroad crossings.

nodes.label: An intersection is any point where traffic paths join or cross, including streets, driveways and parking-lot entrances.

nodes.label: After stopping at an intersection, look both ways again just before moving.

nodes.label: Use particular care just after a light turns green because cross traffic may still try to hurry through.

nodes.label: If your cross-street view is blocked after stopping, creep forward slowly until approaching traffic becomes visible.

nodes.domain: Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

nodes.label: At every railroad approach, reduce speed and look both ways along the tracks for a train.
nodes.domain: Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: A crossing where you have never seen a train must still be checked for an approaching train.
nodes.domain: Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: Cross tracks only when enough room exists beyond them to hold the vehicle.
nodes.domain: Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: At a multitrack crossing, let a passing train move well away before crossing because it can hide another train.

nodes.label: Monitor rear traffic more frequently when the traffic stream is heavy.

nodes.label: Rear checks reveal a following vehicle that is too close or approaching too quickly.
nodes.domain: Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: Rear-traffic checks are especially important before a lane change, slowdown, backing movement or descent of a long or steep hill.
nodes.domain: Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: Before changing lanes, check both the side and the rear for vehicles in the intended lane.
nodes.domain: Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: Lane changing includes merging from an entrance ramp and entering traffic from a curb or shoulder.
nodes.domain: Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: Use both rearview and side mirrors to check whether the target lane is clear.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: Before moving sideways, look over your shoulder toward that direction to check near the vehicle’s rear corners.
nodes.domain: Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

nodes.label: The rear-corner areas invisible through the mirrors are blind spots.

confusable_with.why: Mirrors help check the target lane, but rear-corner blind spots are not visible through them. A mirror check alone does not establish blind-spot clearance.

nodes.domain: Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: Use mirrors while preparing to merge, change lanes or enter the road so you can continue monitoring ahead.
nodes.domain: Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: Check over your shoulder for blind-spot traffic immediately before changing lanes.
nodes.domain: Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: Several quick looks are preferable to one long look away from the road ahead.
nodes.domain: Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: During a lane change, track both the traffic ahead and the traffic in the lane you are entering.
nodes.domain: Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: If there is a lane beyond the one you plan to enter, check it for another driver moving into the same space.
nodes.domain: Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: Motorcyclists, bicyclists and pedestrians can be harder to notice than cars or trucks.
nodes.domain: Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: Be particularly alert for other road users when pulling into the roadway from a curb or driveway.
nodes.domain: Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: Check rear traffic whenever you slow, especially for a sudden slowdown or a stop at an unexpected driveway or parking space.
nodes.domain: Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: Keep backing movements to a minimum because the area behind a vehicle is difficult to see.
nodes.domain: Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: A parking space that lets you drive through can allow a forward departure instead of backing out.
nodes.domain: Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: Before entering the vehicle to back it, check behind for children or low objects hidden from the driver’s seat.
nodes.domain: Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: When backing, the handbook describes resting the right arm on the seatback and turning to look through the rear window.
nodes.domain: Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: Do not rely only on the mirrors while backing because they do not show the area directly behind the vehicle.
nodes.domain: Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: Reverse slowly because controlling the steering is harder while moving backward.
nodes.domain: Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: Use a person outside to help guide a backing movement whenever possible.
nodes.domain: Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: During a long or steep descent, watch the mirrors for vehicles gaining speed behind you.
nodes.domain: Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: On downhill grades, stay alert for large trucks or buses approaching too fast.
nodes.domain: Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning
